りんくる食堂.name: Rinkuru Shokudo
りんくる食堂.desc: A café-like Okinawa soba shop in a renovated former foreigners' house. The signature "Rinkuru soba" is an everything-on-top style bowl with additive-free bonito broth, topped with sea lettuce, sweet chicken, mozuku, and more. Unusual items like mushroom soba and clam soba too.
t: I went to eat here in December 2023 😊 It was during the "13th Okinawa Soba Stamp Rally (2023.10.1–2024.2.29)", so I wanted to eat at a participating shop, but there weren't any nearby, so I decided to eat at this shop, which isn't part of the stamp rally but which I'd been curious about for a while.
Rinkuru Shokudo — it seems to be an Okinawa soba shop in a renovated foreigners' house 😄
Rinkuru Shokudo entrance

If you go a little into the seaward blocks off Route 58 in Chatan Town, there's a neighborhood of foreigners' houses, and this shop has renovated a former foreigners' house into a café-like atmosphere 😁
I went inside and checked the menu.
Menu
Menu
There are lots of kinds of Okinawa soba 😄 "Mushroom soba" and "clam soba" are menu items I'm seeing for the first time, ones other shops don't have.
Menu — this seems to be the side menu for the Okinawa soba 😆
This time I ordered the "Rinkuru soba", which shares the shop's name, sits at the top of the menu, and seems to be the recommendation lol
Rinkuru soba ¥950

The "Rinkuru soba" has arrived 😁 My eyes went to the toppings first. Braised pork belly (sanmai-niku), thinly sliced omelet, mozuku, green onion, sea lettuce (āsa), and chicken — I thought it was like an "everything-on-top" Okinawa soba of the items this shop handles. It reminded me of Futami Soba in Nago City (introduced as a shop that holds its own against the recommended ones) lol

But first, as usual, the soup 😆 Mm, it's a bonito broth soup with a strong bonito flavor. As explained on the menu, they advertise no chemical seasonings, no colorings, and no preservatives, so they seem particular about their ingredients.

However, it reminded me of a recent national news story where a shop selling muffins at some event, with a similar organic mindset, sold them as kid-friendly muffins with no preservatives and half the sugar, but the people who ate them got food poisoning (^0^;)
Scientifically, chemical seasonings have the same components as natural ingredients, so I think you don't really need to worry about them, and extreme, excessive organic thinking calls for caution.
That said, this shop's soup is gentle with no problems at all, so rest assured 😄
Rinkuru soba ¥950
Next I try the noodles. The medium-thick straight noodles are a bit on the soft side.
As for the toppings, first, the sea lettuce has a briny aroma of the sea and is delicious 😆 It reminded me of the "āsa soba" at "Nakamura Soba" in Onna Village lol

I couldn't really tell whether the chicken was chicken tempura, fried chicken, or chicken nanban, but it had a sweetish seasoning and I thought it was very delicious. I thought this topping was a nice new one I'd never seen at other shops 😄 The braised pork belly, however, had a bit of a sinewy texture, which was a shame.

Rating (9.5/15): Simply tasty. The sea lettuce and chicken (tempura? fried? nanban?) toppings in particular were delicious, and I thought they were new toppings. The shop is in a foreigners' house, so I thought tourists can enjoy Okinawa soba in a nice atmosphere too — how about trying it once?

わぁ～家～.name: Waa-ya
わぁ～家～.desc: A diner on the grounds of Roadside Station Yui Yui Kunigami. In a nostalgic interior with checkered tablecloths, enjoy soki soba in an amber-colored soup. Perfect for a break while sightseeing in Yanbaru.
t: This article was created with AI (Claude 3.7 Sonnet), with some parts added by me lol 🍜✨
I ate here in October 2024 😄

This time I went to "Waa-ya" on the grounds of Roadside Station Yui Yui Kunigami in Okuma, Kunigami Village. Kunigami Village is a nature-rich area at the northern tip of Okinawa's main island, surrounded by the Yanbaru forest and beautiful seas, and it's popular as a sightseeing spot too 🌳🌊
Waa-ya

Roadside Station Yui Yui Kunigami is full of local specialties and tourist information, and it's a perfect spot for a break on a drive. "Waa-ya", on its grounds, is a popular shop not only with locals but with tourists too 😄
Inside the shop

When you go inside, the atmosphere feels somehow nostalgic. The tropical-style checkered tablecloths give it warmth. Looking at the menu, there were several Okinawan local dishes, starting with Okinawa soba. This time I decided to order the classic "soki soba" 🍜
Soki soba ¥850
After waiting a while, the "soki soba" was brought out. Medium-thick straight noodles in a clear amber soup, with the soki meat carefully arranged on top. First, as usual, I taste the soup.
Taking a sip of the soup, the pork bone broth had a slight kick, and the saltiness felt somewhat strong.
Next I have the noodles. Medium-thin straight noodles with a somewhat soft texture. They cling well to the soup, but personally I felt they could have a bit more bite.

The soki meat had a light seasoning and was simply tasty, but some parts still had quite a sinewy texture and were hard to eat. From what I heard before, this shop used to use inobuta (wild boar–pig hybrid) meat, but apparently it became hard to source and now it's regular pork. I wanted to try inobuta soki soba for the first time, so that was a little disappointing 😢

There were also several groups of what looked like tourists in the shop, and I could see them enjoying Okinawan food culture. When you make the trip to Kunigami Village, it's a spot where you can enjoy this Okinawa soba along with the nature of Yanbaru 🚗

Rating (9/15): The soup is pork-bone based with a salty kick and simply tasty. The noodles are on the soft side and easy to eat, but the soki meat was a bit sinewy, so it felt like it needed just a little more. If you stop by while sightseeing in Kunigami Village, I think it's worth trying once as a local flavor 😊

わざ家.name: Waza-ya
わざ家.area: Jitchaku, Urasoe (inside the National Theatre Okinawa)
わざ家.desc: A one-of-a-kind shop inside the National Theatre Okinawa. While flying a banner for "the original Ryukyu suba", it offers soy sauce ramen made with medium-thick fresh Okinawa soba noodles, Taiwanese ramen, and even lu rou fan — a shop of "ramen made with Okinawa soba noodles".
t: *This article was created with AI (Claude Haiku 4.5), with some parts added and updated by me 😆
I went to eat here in January 2025 😁😊
The National Theatre Okinawa in Jitchaku, Urasoe City. Inside this facility, where you can fully enjoy Okinawa's traditional culture, there's a slightly unusual Okinawa soba shop. That's "Waza-ya".
Waza-ya (located inside the National Theatre Okinawa)
Waza-ya (located inside the National Theatre Okinawa)
Waza-ya (located inside the National Theatre Okinawa)
Meal ticket machine
🎭This time I got the "soy sauce ramen with lu rou fan" set. The banner proudly says "Ryukyu suba", so this definitely counts toward my Okinawa soba tour 😄
Inside the shop

When you enter the National Theatre Okinawa building, you see, a more modern and refined space than you'd imagine opens up. The thick bare-concrete pillars are striking, the ceilings are high, and the atmosphere is open. Like a café — no, even more contemporary, yet a mysterious space with a faint scent of the Ryukyus. 🪟Through the big windows you can see Okinawa's nature. Waza-ya, you see, has set up shop in a corner of this space. In front, a banner reading "The Original Ryukyu Suba Waza-ya" flutters prominently. Ordering is by ticket machine, and there's a really extensive lineup, from Okinawa soba–related items to Taiwanese ramen, and even gyoza and rice dishes.
Soy sauce ramen with lu rou fan ¥1,030

Well, here comes the "soy sauce ramen". 😍The soup seems to be based on rich pork bone, kombu, and bonito broth. But I couldn't even tell if it was soy sauce flavored — it's somehow complex, with a pretty rich, heavy taste. 🍲What I'm most curious about, you see, is this soup. Is it an Okinawa soba–style broth, or authentic ramen? The line between them is blurry. It's distinctive, but feels like something different from regular Okinawa soba.
Soy sauce ramen with lu rou fan ¥1,030

The biggest highlight, you see, is these noodles! 🤩They use medium-thick Okinawa soba noodles. Just from looking at them, you see, you can tell they're chewy. When you actually eat them, you see, they have the springy texture of fresh noodles. The noodles alone are completely Okinawa soba. This part is really well done. The toppings are basically ramen 😅 A big slice of chashu sits there prominently, and there's a soft-boiled egg on top too.

The lu rou fan, in the tradition of Taiwanese ramen, is pork simmered down in a miso flavor, piled generously over white rice. There's mitsuba on top too. This lu rou fan also has a pretty robust seasoning, and eating it together with the ramen boosts the satisfaction in one go. Overall the volume is more than enough. There's so much that I got a little worried whether I could finish it all by myself.

If I were to describe Waza-ya in one phrase, you see, it'd be "ramen made with Okinawa soba noodles". It's not completely Okinawa soba, but it's not completely ramen either. If anything, maybe it's more like "Okinawa soba in the shape of ramen". The banner saying "Ryukyu suba" also conveys that spirit of challenge. 😄It's precisely because the location, you see, is inside a cultural facility called the National Theatre Okinawa that a concept like this "fusion of tradition and novelty" might be so naturally accepted. It has an atmosphere where not only tourists but locals too can drop by casually.
Rating (9/15): It's ramen with Okinawa soba noodles (^0^;) Simply tasty.

アグーそば処 ひかり食堂.name: Agu Soba-dokoro Hikari Shokudo
アグーそば処 ひかり食堂.desc: A two-in-one shop: Hikari Shokudo by day and Shokuraku Shubo Juria by night. Its feature is that you can choose the soup, rich with Agu pork broth, from three types: rich, light, or blend. The signature Agu Hikari soba is topped with both braised pork belly and soft-bone pork ribs.
t: I went to eat here in March 2025 😄
This time I'm introducing "-Agu Soba-dokoro- Hikari Shokudo" in Meido, Okinawa City 😊
-Agu Soba-dokoro- Hikari Shokudo

The exterior has a calm design based on black, and at the entrance a lantern reading "Juria" catches the eye. In fact, this is a two-in-one shop that serves Okinawa soba as "Hikari Shokudo" during the day and transforms into an izakaya called "Shokuraku Shubo Juria" at night 🍺 It's open across a wide range of hours: 10:00 AM–2:00 PM for lunch and 5:00 PM–1:00 AM at night. It seems they're on Uber Eats too.
Meal ticket machine near the entrance
Menu posted on the wall

Ordering is by ticket machine. Looking at the menu, there's a full lineup of Agu soba items 😆 This time I ordered the shop's top recommendation, the "Agu Hikari soba (¥950)". It's a hearty bowl with both braised pork belly and soft-bone ribs. The interesting point of this soba is that you can choose the soup from three types: rich, light, or blend 🐷 When I asked the staff for a recommendation, they said "The blend is recommended", so I chose the blend without hesitation!
Agu Hikari soba (blend soup) ¥950

The "Agu Hikari soba" that appeared after a short wait is served in a black bowl and looks pretty good ✨ First, a sip of the soup. The Agu pork broth comes through firmly — full-bodied yet not heavy. I could also sense what seemed to be a bonito broth flavor, giving it a taste unique to the blend. The best of both rich and light, I guess? 😋
Agu Hikari soba (blend soup) ¥950
Next I try the noodles 🙏 The noodles are medium-thin and straight, with a softish texture.

The toppings — braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) and soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki) — come in big, hearty chunks, and it's quite filling 😄 The seasoning is on the light side, perhaps to make the most of the Agu pork's own umami. The soft-bone pork ribs are tender, but some parts still had a bit of a sinewy texture. The braised pork belly has a strong sinewy texture with real chew, a properly meaty texture that's very filling 🐷
Right inside the entrance it's suddenly private rooms (^0^;)

The interior has a private-room layout, built to suit the nighttime izakaya business. But because right inside the entrance is the wall of a private room, you can't really see the staff... At first I was a little confused about who to call out to (lol) 😂 But once you've ordered at the ticket machine, all that's left is to wait leisurely, so no problem. On the wall there was something like a certificate for Okinawa-produced Agu pork, which shows their commitment to ingredients.

I've been around a fair number of shops that feature Agu pork, but being able to choose the soup style from three types, so you can customize it to your taste, is a nice point 😊 It was a simply tasty bowl!
Rating (9/15): Simply tasty Agu soba. Being able to choose the soup style is its distinctive feature 😊

アワセそば食堂.name: Awase Soba Shokudo
アワセそば食堂.desc: A long-established popular shop whose signature is a perfectly balanced soup where you can taste both bonito and pork bone at the same time. You can choose homemade flat or thin noodles, and the No. 1 most popular item is the sanmai-niku soba. The parking lot fills up at Sunday lunchtime.
t: I ate here in May 2023 😄
I came at lunchtime on a Sunday, but the parking lot was full (・・) After waiting a little, one space opened up, so I managed to get in 😊
Menu (their commitments are explained 😊)
Menu (the No. 1 to No. 3 most popular items are explained 😄)

Looking at the menu, I ordered the No. 1 most popular "sanmai-niku soba". You can choose flat or thin noodles, and when I asked the staff, they recommended the flat noodles, saying "the old-fashioned flat noodles are ordered a lot", so I ordered with flat noodles.
Sanmai-niku soba (large) ¥880
As always, I go around to shops that catch my interest with no prior information, so I took a first sip of the soup wondering, "Bonito broth?" "Pork bone broth?" 😄

The moment I drank it: "?" I couldn't immediately tell the base flavor of the soup, so I took another sip to check. I can taste bonito broth, and I can also taste pork bone broth — a soup flavor unlike any I've had so far.

At Okinawa soba shops up to now, even with a bonito-and-pork blended broth, it's usual for one flavor to be stronger, but at Awase Soba Shokudo you can taste both flavors, and I thought it was a perfect balance.
The homemade flat noodles have a soft bite. The braised pork belly topping is also tender and delicious 😄

Rating (9/15): Simply tasty. The soup lets you taste both bonito and pork bone, something other shops don't have. A long-established popular shop bustling with local customers. They also accept PayPay, and it was the first Okinawa soba shop where I got a receipt, so I plan to turn it into money using the method in another article ("[Points hacking] How to turn receipts into money (small change) (super steady-effort type)") 😄

シラノ.name: Shirano
シラノ.desc: A stylish, Western-style "Okinawa Soba and Pan Shop" run by an owner with a French cooking background. Starting with an appetizer of garlic toast, its soki soba in bonito soup is distinctive, letting you change the flavor with citrus condiments made from shikuwasa and tankan.
t: I ate here in March 2024 😄 I learned about this shop from the newspaper lol
Okinawa Soba and Pan Shop Shirano
Okinawa Soba and Pan Shop Shirano
Okinawa Soba and Pan Shop Shirano
What country's architecture does this look like? It's Western-style 😄 Different from the Okinawa soba shops I usually go to 😄
Near the entrance in front of the shop (it's in a peaceful, rural kind of place)
The entrance in front of the shop (it's on slightly elevated ground)

According to the newspaper article, it had only just opened in November 2023. The owner seems to be a chef with a French cooking background. That's why the building is Western-style like this — because of the French background 😁
When I went inside, since it was lunchtime, there were quite a lot of customers. The interior is Western-style, but the moment I entered there was a lovely smell of bonito broth 🤤
It seems to be based on a bonito and pork bone broth, but from the smell drifting through the shop, I thought the bonito was dominant lol
The counter seats inside (Western-style, isn't it)

I forgot to take a photo of the menu, but I ordered the "soki soba". Among the other items there was also "clam-broth Okinawa soba", which I thought looked delicious, but I was told it was "sold out" (^0^;) There was also a menu item called "spice curry soba", which also looked delicious and I hesitated, but I thought I should order the classic here after all, so I went with the "soki soba" 😁
Appetizer garlic toast
Before the Okinawa soba, garlic toast came out with "Here's your appetizer". Other shops don't have this style — just as the sign says, it really is an "Okinawa Soba and Pan Shop" 😁
The crispy toasted bread has a good garlic kick and is simply tasty.
Soki soba ¥850 (other shops don't have citrus condiments)

First I taste the soup. It's mainly bonito, combined with pork bone broth, and the soup seems to take cues from French technique. It's a soup that fills the shop with a lovely aroma, so I took a sip with high expectations.
As expected, the bonito comes through, and it's a simply tasty soup.
Soki soba ¥850
Next I have the noodles. They're homemade aged noodles, apparently rested for five days after being made before they're finished. Thin noodles, and I thought these were also just ordinary.
While enjoying the soup, noodles, and soki, in the second half I changed the flavor with condiments made from shikuwasa and tankan (Okinawan citrus), something other shops don't have.
A citrusy freshness gets added to the bonito broth soup, and I thought it was a new flavor, but they go well together — delicious.

Rating (9/15): A shop with a stylish Western-style exterior and interior. How about trying Okinawa soba made by an owner with a French cooking background at least once 😁 The citrus condiments go well with the bonito-forward soup, so why not try them? The location is peaceful and quiet, so you can enjoy your meal at a relaxed pace.
